newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: THOMSON UPGRADES COUNTRY RATING TO BB.
newsitem.headline: THOMSON UPGRADES COUNTRY RATING TO BB.

text.p: Rating agency Thomson Bankwatch on Wednesday said it has raised its sovereign rating for Lithuania to BB from BB-.
The agency in a statement cited improved economic performance resulting from national stabilisation policies.

"Not only has economic activity accelerated in recent years but inflation has fallen dramatically, down to 13.1 percent at the end of last year, marking its lowest level since independence," Thomson director of sovereign risk Betty Starkey said in a statement.
She said that interest rates had fallen and that the currency board has kept the litas currency stable.
"The government has pursued a relatively cautious fiscal policy, which has led to substantial expenditure reductions," she added.
She said that further efforts were needed to bolster fiscal finances but that progress to date has been noteworthy.

The agency also noted that Lithuania was boosting exports to the West, away from the former Soviet Union. The reorientation in trade along with the stabilisation efforts meant that GDP was forecast to grow by three and four percent this year.

"Politically, Lithuania remains among the most stable of the three Baltic states, with a more predictable domestic political environment and fewer changes in the top rungs of leadership," Starkey said.
She said the current government had a majority, which should allow it to continue reforms, including privatisation.
"Acceleration of these efforts will be critical to sustaining the country's economic recovery," Starkey added.
